incidents.victim: Multiple sectors globally (healthcare, education, government, finance)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware ecosystem (Fox Tempest malware-signing service, used by Vanilla Tempest/Rhysida and INC/Qilin/Akira affiliates)
incidents.vector: Fox Tempest fraudulently abused Microsoft Artifact Signing to issue valid short-lived code-signing certificates, letting ransomware affiliates distribute signed malware via malvertising, SEO poisoning, and fake software downloads (e.g., counterfeit Teams installers).
incidents.impact: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit seized signspace[.]cloud, took down hundreds of attacker VMs hosted on Cloudzy, and revoked over 1,000 fraudulent certificates. The service had operated since May 2025 and enabled deployment of Rhysida, Oyster, Lumma Stealer, and Vidar against thousands of victims worldwide; Microsoft observed Fox Tempest already attempting to migrate customers to a replacement service.

incidents.vector: Denial-of-service attack exploiting a previously unknown, undocumented vulnerability in Huawei enterprise router software; no CVE has been filed or public warning issued in the ten months since the incident.
incidents.impact: Nationwide collapse of Luxembourg's telecoms network for over three hours on July 23, 2025 — disrupting mobile, landline, and emergency 112 calls for potentially hundreds of thousands of residents. Details disclosed publicly by The Record on May 19, 2026.

incidents.victim: npm software ecosystem (hundreds of packages and downstream consumers)
incidents.vector: Self-replicating worm dropped into hundreds of npm packages; a pre-install hook fires before any other step on the developer machine or CI runner, harvesting GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys, cloud-provider credentials, and DB strings, then uses the pipeline's own publishing identity to push poisoned versions of additional packages under legitimate maintainer names.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of npm packages compromised in this latest wave; persistent OS-level backdoors installed that survive package uninstall. Worm source code was released the prior week on a hacking forum, fueling broader copycat activity across the developer ecosystem.

incidents.attacker: Unknown (researcher disclosure, some flaws already being exploited in the wild)
incidents.vector: Researcher "Nightmare Eclipse" publicly disclosed three new Windows flaws — YellowKey (BitLocker bypass via weaponized USB inserted before WinRE boot), GreenPlasma, and MiniPlasma — plus a PoC against a vulnerability Microsoft had marked as patched in 2020.
incidents.impact: YellowKey lets anyone with physical access fully bypass BitLocker on encrypted laptops without credentials, PIN, or TPM bypass. Some of the disclosed flaws are already being exploited, and at least one is in CISA's KEV catalog. Patches are not yet available for several.

incidents.vector: Cross-site scripting flaw (CVE-2026-42897) in Outlook Web Access — attacker emails a crafted message; when opened in OWA arbitrary JavaScript runs in the browser context, enabling spoofing, mailbox access, and session-token theft.
incidents.impact: Active in-the-wild exploitation with no patch available four days after disclosure. Affects Exchange Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. CISA added CVE-2026-42897 to its KEV catalog on May 15; the Belgian CCB warned successful exploitation could give attackers access to victim mailboxes, session tokens, and mailbox rules.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — no evidence of malicious access; exposure flagged by GitGuardian researcher
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor maintained a public GitHub repository ("Private-CISA") containing credentials, build/deploy artifacts, and internal system documentation. The administrator had disabled GitHub's default secret-push protection.
incidents.impact: Exposed credentials authenticated to three highly privileged AWS GovCloud accounts and included plain-text creds for CISA's internal "artifactory" code-package repository. Security researchers called it one of the most egregious US government data leaks in recent history. The repo was taken down only after KrebsOnSecurity inquiries.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (tracked by Microsoft as Storm-2949)
incidents.vector: Social engineering of IT and senior-leadership users via fraudulent IT-helpdesk calls during attacker-initiated Self-Service Password Reset; victims approved MFA prompts believing they were doing a routine reset. Attacker reset passwords, re-enrolled Microsoft Authenticator to their own device, then used legitimate Azure management features (publishxml/action, Kudu) and Microsoft Graph to enumerate and pivot.
incidents.impact: Full-spectrum cloud breach spanning Microsoft 365 (OneDrive, SharePoint), Azure App Services, Key Vaults, Storage, and SQL. Mass downloads of sensitive IT, VPN, and production data via the OneDrive web UI and custom Python scripts; lateral movement into multiple Azure subscriptions.

incidents.victim: US gas stations (fuel storage tank monitoring)
incidents.vector: Exploited automatic tank gauge (ATG) systems that were internet-exposed without password protection.
incidents.impact: Attackers tampered with displayed fuel-level readings at US gas stations but did not alter actual fuel levels; no operational disruption to fuel delivery reported. CNN attributed the activity to Iran in the context of the ongoing US/Israel-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz tensions.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized party obtained a leaked token granting access to Grafana Labs' GitHub environment and downloaded the company's source code.
incidents.impact: Full codebase downloaded by extortion group CoinbaseCartel; Grafana refused to pay the ransom, citing FBI guidance. The company stated no customer data, personal information, or customer-system operations were affected, and compromised credentials have been invalidated.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia, and the UK
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (BlackFile, tracked by Google/Mandiant as UNC6671)
incidents.vector: High-volume voice phishing (vishing) to employees' personal phones impersonating IT/helpdesk, paired with adversary-in-the-middle credential capture against lookalike SSO portals; attackers harvest MFA codes in real time, then immediately enroll attacker-controlled MFA devices to lock out the user. Followed by scripted exfiltration using python-requests/PowerShell against Microsoft Graph and SharePoint with stolen session cookies.
incidents.impact: Mass theft of corporate data from Microsoft 365 and Okta environments (SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce, Zendesk). In one engagement, over one million files were exfiltrated from a single victim. Extortion includes Tox/Session ransom demands, swatting of executives, and Gmail-based mailbox flooding when victims do not engage.

incidents.attacker: State-suspected espionage group (tracked by Cisco Talos as UAT-8616; infrastructure overlaps with Operational Relay Box networks)
incidents.vector: Active in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart) and SD-WAN Manager (formerly vManage), giving unauthenticated remote attackers administrative privileges. A separate set of actors is also chaining the older February 2026 SD-WAN vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122) using the public ZeroZenX PoC and its associated JSP webshell ("XenShell").
incidents.impact: Limited but confirmed exploitation by a sophisticated actor; post-compromise deployment of webshells and tooling on SD-WAN management-plane appliances. Talos urges immediate patching per Cisco's advisory.
